Global Nourish Corp - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Nourish Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Nourish Corp's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Michael Thornton, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael.

Michael Thornton (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: organic revenue growth overall and by region, e-commerce sales growth and its contribution to total revenue, updates on M&A activity and portfolio management, and EPS guidance and key assumptions.

First, regarding organic revenue growth: we achieved a robust 6.8% increase overall, accelerating from prior quarters, driven by balanced volume, pricing, and mix shifts across our resilient brands in snacks and beverages.

Second, concerning e-commerce sales growth: this channel surged 48% year-over-year to represent over 11% of total revenue, highlighting our omnichannel momentum and higher-margin potential.

Third, in terms of updates on M&A activity and portfolio management: we've executed strategic bolt-ons totaling nearly $3 billion while divesting non-core assets, sharpening our focus on high-ROIC health and wellness categories.

Finally, looking at EPS guidance and key assumptions: we're reaffirming our full-year outlook with solid growth expected from productivity, mix improvements, and controlled costs.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Michael. As Michael mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $2.8 billion, representing a 7% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 24.0%, impacted by moderating commodity inflation offset by productivity savings and favorable product mix. Operating income was $420 million, and earnings per share were $0.68. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

To give you deeper insight into the four areas Michael highlighted, let me expand on each, starting with our organic revenue growth, which remains the cornerstone of our performance and a clear testament to the resilience of our core brands here at Global Nourish Corp in the Food & Beverage sector. For the quarter, we delivered overall organic revenue growth of 6.8%, accelerating from 4.9% in the prior quarter and surpassing our guided range of 4% to 6%. This marks our strongest quarterly organic print in over a year and a half, driven by a balanced mix of 2.3% volume growth, 3.1% pricing actions, and 1.4% favorable product mix—all underpinned by our disciplined execution amid persistent inflationary headwinds.

To put this in context, the global F&B industry faced moderating consumer demand in staples but robust tailwinds in premium and health-oriented categories. Industry data shows snacking and ready-to-drink beverages grew 5% to 7% globally, while traditional carbonated soft drinks flatlined. Our portfolio—spanning powerhouse brands like NourishJuice, our number-two plant-based juice line; NourishBar snack bars, competing with leading protein options; and EnergizePro energy drinks, gaining share against major players—positioned us perfectly to capture these shifts. Year-to-date, organic growth stands at 5.9%, keeping us on track for our full-year target of 5% to 7%.

Breaking this down by region reflects both macroeconomic variances and our tailored go-to-market strategies. North America, which accounts for 47% of total revenue, led the way with organic growth of 8.2%, up from 6.1% last quarter. This was fueled by 3.8% pricing—strategically layered to offset 4% to 5% COGS inflation in commodities like cocoa and almond milk—coupled with 2.9% volume gains from our Health Momentum initiative. In beverages, NourishJuice saw 12% household penetration growth in the Northeast, driven by expanded distribution in major retailers, where low-sugar, fortified variants now represent 35% of SKUs. Snacks contributed strongly, with NourishBar up 15% at constant currency, benefiting from e-commerce acceleration—Amazon sales volumes rose 28% year-over-year via fulfillment optimizations and subscription bundles. Mix was a tailwind at 1.5%, as premium protein bars outpaced legacy cookies by a wide margin. Challenges persist in certain areas where at-home baking cannibalized ready-to-eat snacks, but our new co-manufacturing agreement is ramping to add incremental volumes in the second half.

EMEA, 28% of revenue, posted solid organic growth of 4.7%, a sequential improvement despite softer consumer sentiment in key markets. Pricing at 2.9% aligned with regional inflation, while volumes grew 1.2%—led by EnergizePro's 18% surge in functional energy drinks, capturing share in the sizable RTD category. In France and Iberia, our dairy-alternative push with NourishJuice oat milks gained significant market share versus competitors, thanks to sustainability certifications on 80% of sourcing. Mix improved from premiumization, though FX headwinds shaved off some reported growth. Strategically, we're doubling down on direct-to-consumer via our app, which drove a substantial portion of incremental sales through personalized subscriptions.

Asia-Pacific, 15% of revenue, was our growth engine at 9.6% organic, propelled by ramps in China and India. Volumes jumped 4.1%, with NourishBar's savory rice crackers exploding 25% in urban India amid the snacking boom—now a top player in the market. Pricing was moderated at 2.8% to preserve affordability in mass channels. Our innovation pipeline shone: the launch of low-cal RTD teas in Southeast Asia hit strong repeat purchase rates early on. Mix reflected premium functional beverages, now nearly 30% of regional sales. Tailwinds include urbanization and rising e-commerce penetration, but we're vigilant on input volatility, mitigated by hedging.

Latin America and other emerging markets, 10% of revenue, delivered 12.4% organic growth, with standout performance in Brazil and Mexico. This was volume-led at 5.6%, as EnergizePro gained distribution in key networks, tapping a fast-growing energy drink market. Pricing countered ag-input inflation, while mix came from shifting to fortified juices amid nutrition mandates. Our localized production partnerships cut lead times significantly, boosting shelf-life-sensitive products.

Looking ahead, these trends affirm our growth framework: relentless pricing discipline targeting over 3% annually, volume via innovation with several new SKUs launching soon, and mix through portfolio health—we're pruning low-margin legacy items. Supply chain initiatives like AI-driven demand forecasting have improved fill rates globally, adding meaningful growth. Risks include commodity spikes and potential recessionary pullback, but our recurring revenue provides ballast. In summary, this 6.8% underscores our competitive moat.

Moving to e-commerce sales growth and its contribution to total revenue, this continues to be one of our brightest growth stories and a key pillar in our omnichannel strategy amid shifting consumer behaviors in Food & Beverage. In Q3, e-commerce sales reached $285 million, marking a robust 48% year-over-year increase and representing 11.2% of our total net revenue of $2.8 billion—up from 7.1% in the prior-year period and 9.8% in the previous quarter. This outperformance underscores the structural shift industry-wide, where e-commerce penetration in grocery and F&B has climbed to 13-15% of total U.S. sales, driven by younger consumers prioritizing convenience, personalization, and sustainability.

Key drivers include our direct-to-consumer platforms, which delivered 62% year-over-year growth to $145 million, fueled by a 28% rise in average order value to $68, thanks to targeted bundling of high-margin products like our Organic Protein Shakes and Ready-to-Eat Meal Kits. Basket sizes expanded as customers pair staples like nut butters with impulse functional beverages.

On the marketplace side, partnerships have been transformative. Sales through Amazon and similar surged 55% to $92 million, benefiting from exclusive launches like our Zero-Sugar Energy Drinks, which captured significant share quickly. Integrations with delivery services added another $48 million, with a 35% uptick in same-day orders—critical where shoppers expect fast fulfillment.

Regionally, North America accounts for 78% of e-comm revenue at $222 million, up 52% year-over-year, propelled by urban density and logistics efficiencies. In EMEA, we're up 39% to $42 million, or 15% of regional sales, thanks to optimized partnerships for perishables, reducing waste through AI forecasting. APAC is the fastest grower at 112% to $21 million, primarily via major platforms in China, favoring our premium snacks—though watchful of macro headwinds.

We've invested heavily in our e-comm stack, boosting conversion rates and repeat purchases via advanced personalization. Our subscription program now has 1.2 million members, generating substantial recurring revenue with high retention.

Strategically, e-commerce is reshaping our P&L—gross margins here expanded significantly due to lower fees and better turns. We're leveraging data to refine forecasts, cutting stockouts and advancing sustainability. Looking forward, we expect it to contribute 13-14% of full-year revenue, with strong Q4 growth.

Now, turning to updates on our M&A activity and portfolio management, which continue to be cornerstones of our strategy to drive sustainable, high-ROIC growth. We've maintained a disciplined approach amid macroeconomic headwinds—persistent inflation in commodities like cocoa and dairy at 8-10% year-over-year, supply chain disruptions from Red Sea rerouting, and shifting consumer preferences toward health & wellness, premiumization, and sustainability. Our portfolio is now 65% weighted toward resilient categories like snacks, plant-based proteins, and functional beverages, up from 52% three years ago, positioning us for mid-single-digit organic growth through the cycle.

Recent M&A executions totaled $2.8 billion in deployable capital across three transactions this fiscal year. Our bolt-on strategy targets tuck-in opportunities in high-growth sub-segments with strong brand equity and supply chain complementarity, aiming for 3-5% accretion to adjusted EPS within 18 months.

Key acquisitions: First, in February, we closed the $1.2 billion acquisition of VitaGreen Foods, a leader in premium plant-based snacks with brands like GreenBite veggie crisps and NutriPod protein bites. This adds $450 million in trailing revenue at a 22% EBITDA margin—above our Snacks division's blended rate—and expands our U.S. market share in the $25 billion plant-based snacks category from 4% to 7%. Integration is ahead of plan: We've realized $45 million in run-rate synergies through procurement savings on pea protein and almonds—15% cost reduction—and cross-selling into our retail footprint alongside NourishCrunch. North America contributes 70% of VitaGreen's sales, but we're accelerating APAC penetration, launching in China via Tmall, targeting 20% growth amid Asia's 12% CAGR plant-based market.

Second, our $650 million tuck-in of EuroBev Innovations bolsters functional beverages. EuroBev's HydraBoost line—zero-sugar, electrolyte-infused RTDs with adaptogens—brings $220 million in revenue and aligns with premium hydration growing 15% globally. We've integrated their German facility into our EMEA hub, yielding $30 million in synergies from shared lines and 12% lower logistics. This positions us against competitors, with early 8% market share gains in Western Europe.

Third, a $150 million investment in Latin America's FrutaPure purees enhances away-from-home exposure, adding 10% to our LatAm portfolio for B2B quick-service sales.

On divestitures, we've sold $1.1 billion in non-core assets. The $900 million sale of legacy Dairy Essentials—commodity milk powders and ice creams—generated a $250 million after-tax gain and freed $400 million in working capital from volatile dairy chains with 11% inflation. Post-sale, Nutrition & Plant-Based is 28% of revenue, margins up 220 basis points to 24.5%.

Portfolio management uses our AI-powered PortOptix platform, scoring SKUs on brand health, velocity, and sustainability. We've rationalized 15% of legacy items—like sugary sodas—driving 2.5% margin expansion. Initiatives include blockchain traceability for 80% of supply chain, reducing recalls 40%, and predictive analytics improving inventory turns from 8.2x to 9.5x.

Regionally: North America (55%) saw 6% organic growth from M&A, outpacing category; EMEA (25%) 10% from premiumization and regulations; APAC (15%) targeting India snacks; LatAm (5%) 12% growth hedging inflation.

Forward, $3-4 billion pipeline for 4-6 deals in health adjacencies, leverage below 2.5x, ROIC over 15%.

Finally, on EPS guidance and key assumptions for FY2025, with Q3 adjusted EPS contributing to year-to-date strength, we're guiding to adjusted diluted EPS of $2.65 to $2.85, or 10% to 18% growth at midpoint. This reflects conviction in category fundamentals, disciplined pricing, productivity, and high-margin growth in plant-based snacks and zero-sugar beverages.

Revenue outlook: 5% to 7% organic growth—3% pricing, 2-4% volume/mix. North America flat to 2%, offset by e-commerce to 15%; Europe 6-8% from premium alt-dairy; APAC/LatAm 10-12%. FX drag 1%.

Gross margins expand 100-150bps to 24.5% from benign commodities—corn down 5%, hedged exposure—$180 million productivity via supply chain AI and automation, premium mix.

SG&A flat to down slightly at 16.5%, with investments in marketing and R&D for upcycled ingredients. Interest flat, tax 23.5%, shares 285 million post buybacks. Capex $450 million, FCF $850-950 million supporting dividends.

Assumes modest M&A, better-for-you transitions. Risks: cocoa volatility, consumer spending; upside in e-comm, alt-proteins.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for adjusted EPS of $2.65 to $2.85 alongside 5% to 7% organic growth.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Doe with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

John Doe (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of recent commodity inflation on your business?

Michael Thornton (CEO):
Good morning, John. We've navigated commodity inflation effectively through a combination of targeted pricing actions averaging 3% across regions, comprehensive hedging covering 70% of exposures, and productivity gains from our supply chain optimizations. This allowed us to protect margins while maintaining competitive positioning in premium categories, where consumers are willing to trade up despite pressures.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Jane Smith (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for functional beverages and what is the expected market share impact?

Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Jane. Our functional beverages, bolstered by the EuroBev acquisition and HydraBoost line, are a priority with plans for expanded distribution in North America and APAC, alongside new zero-sugar variants launching next quarter. We expect this to drive 10-15% market share gains in key regions like Western Europe and urban Asia, contributing 2-3% to overall organic growth through premium pricing and subscription models.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Lee with Citi. Please proceed.

Bob Lee (Citi):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Bob, thanks for the question. We're leveraging AI-driven predictive analytics and blockchain traceability across 80% of our chain to improve forecasting accuracy and reduce risks—fill rates at 98%, inventory turns up to 9.5x. Post-acquisitions, we've optimized routes and shared facilities, cutting costs 12%, while local sourcing in LatAm and APAC hedges disruptions like Red Sea issues. This has made us more resilient, with recall risks down 40%.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Alice Wong with Barclays. Please proceed.

Alice Wong (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Alice, our outlook remains constructive, with Q4 organic growth in the 6-8% range building on Q3 momentum, driven by holiday e-commerce acceleration to 14% mix, continued M&A synergies, and gross margin tailwinds from easing inputs. We'll deliver at the midpoint of our EPS guidance through execution, while monitoring consumer trends and commodities closely.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Michael for closing remarks.

Michael Thornton (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in Global Nourish Corp. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
